chunks: Hareez said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the muhsan. He said:
'The one who commits adultery/fornication while he has with him what makes him needless of it.'

key_terms.الْمُحْصَنِ: muhsan: the married/protected person whose penalty for adultery is stoning rather than lashes; from the root h-s-n (fortification/protection), referring to the legal protection of marriage
key_terms.يَزْنِي: zina: unlawful sexual intercourse (adultery or fornication), one of the major hudud offenses in Islamic law
key_terms.يُغْنِيهِ: yughnihi: makes him needless/sufficient; refers to having a lawful spouse available to fulfil sexual needs

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia definition of muhsan (married person) in relation to the punishment for adultery in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith provides Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) definition of al-muhsan — the legally married person whose punishment for zina (unlawful sexual intercourse) is the severe hadd of stoning (rajm), as opposed to lashes. The Imam defines the muhsan not merely by the legal contract of marriage but by actual access to a lawful spouse: the one who commits zina while possessing what would have made it unnecessary (i.e., a spouse available to fulfill their needs). This definition was significant in classical Islamic jurisprudence because it conditioned the harshest penalty on a higher standard of culpability — the person had a lawful outlet but chose transgression regardless.
word_analysis: makes him needless of it / suffices him

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Hareyz who said, 
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the married man, so he<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘The one who commits adultery and with him is what makes him to be needless of it’.
